etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin violātus, past participle of violāre (“treat with violence, whether bodily or mental”), from vīs (“strength, power, force, violence”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To break or disregard (a rule or convention).

quote.text: That Antonia whom you violated, was your Sister! That Elvira whom you murdered, gave you birth! Tremble, abandoned Hypocrite! Inhuman Parricide! Incestuous Ravisher!

definitions.definition: (transitive, prison slang) To cite (a person) for a parole violation.

quote.text: If you don't have a job, you can't pay the money, then you get violated and have to go back to prison.

quote.citation: 2014, Juanita Díaz-Cotto, Chicana Lives and Criminal Justice: Voices from El Barrio, page 165:
quote.text: Estela: Well, they'd take me to jail, I'd violate, and I go to prison. And maybe I get violated for six months, eight months . . . maybe 30 days, 60 days . . . You know, whatever the parole officer recommended for me, I got.
